Exercise A

A Weekend in London

Read the text, then choose the correct article for each gap.

Before you read — optional, not marked
This is just to get you thinking — you can leave it empty and it does not count towards your score.
Read and complete

Last summer, my friend and I took a train to London for the weekend. We arrived at the station at noon and walked to our hotel. It was small hotel near the river.

In the afternoon, we visited the British Museum. We spent two hours looking at Egyptian collection. After that, we had ice cream in the park.

The next day, we went to Oxford Street and did some shopping. I bought book about London's history. In the evening, we saw musical in the West End. It was a wonderful trip!

Exercise B

Indefinite vs. definite article

Choose a, an or the for each gap.

Complete the sentences
1. There is new café on my street. café serves great coffee.
2. She wants to be engineer when she grows up.
3. Can you close window? It's cold in here.
4. I saw dog in the park. It was chasing ball.
5. My brother is tallest person in our family.
6. I need to buy umbrella — it looks like rain.
Exercise C

The or no article?

Choose the or — (no article) for each gap.

Complete the sentences
1. Water is essential for life.
2. water in this bottle tastes strange.
3. She loves music, especially jazz.
4. music at the party was too loud.
5. I usually have breakfast at 7 o'clock.
6. breakfast she cooked this morning was delicious.
7. He goes to school by bus every day.
8. school on Park Road has a swimming pool.
Exercise D

Describe your neighbourhood

Write 6–8 sentences describing where you live to a new classmate who has never visited. Use a/an for things you mention for the first time, the for specific places you both know, and no article for general ideas.

Your description
Try to use all four article choices: a, an, the, and no article (zero article). Aim for at least 60 words.
